title: Pharmacy Administrator
description: The successful applicant will support a wide range of pharmacy workflows including prescription administration, patient recall programmes and long-term condition clinics. You will act as a key point of contact for patients, community pharmacies and external organisations enquiring about prescriptions. This role brings the opportunity to assist in co-ordinating medication reviews, support audit programmes and manage patient recall systems. To thrive in this role, you will enjoy working in a fast-paced environment with multiple competing priorities. You will possess excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively with patients and healthcare professionals. You will be committed to delivering excellent patient care and able to work both independently and as part of a team. The successful candidate will demonstrate a professional, flexible, and friendly manner. As well as being organised, applicants should have strong IT skills with experience of working with confidential information. Experience of EMIS web and a good understanding of medical terminology is advantageous. As a training practice, we offer a supportive environment with opportunities for learning and development within a growing multidisciplinary pharmacy team. Responsibilities The following are the core responsibilities of the Pharmacy team administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels. Prescription administration and medicines management Patient recall and service coordination Administration for medicines optimisation and clinical pharmacy support Audit, quality improvement and safety Training and team support Process repeat prescription requests received by phone, email, post, slips and the online access system, in accordance with practice protocol and standard operating procedures. Generate requests for non-repeat medications on behalf of patients, obtaining additional information where required. Manage and coordinate weekly prescription workflows to ensure timely processing of prescriptions. Ensure prescription requests are processed within agreed timescales. Escalate urgent prescription requests to the Clinical Pharmacy Team or duty GP as appropriate. Support electronic Repeat Dispensing (eRD) initiatives and encourage suitable patients to use eRD and synchronised medication collections Actively encourage patients to reconcile medications to facilitate monthly collections and electronic repeat dispensing. Act upon prescription compliance issues, liaising with the appropriate clinician. Have oversight of community pharmacy emergency supplies, escalating to the clinical pharmacy team when necessary. Build good working relationships with local Pharmacies to help enable our prescription service. Check emails regularly and deal with them appropriately. Patient recall and service coordination: Maintain medication review recall systems and invite patients for reviews in line with practice procedures. Manage medication review recall lists, including sending invitations, booking appointments and following up non-responders. Liaise with the Pharmacy Technician team regarding any monitoring requirements prior to medication reviews and arrange appointments or investigations as directed. Coordinate recalls for annual medication reviews, long-term condition reviews and pharmacist-led clinics. Book, rearrange and manage appointments for pharmacy-led services. Coordinate spirometry appointments and six-monthly heart failure recall programmes. Support the administration and management of the practice blood pressure monitor loan scheme. Maintain accurate records of recalls, appointments and patient communications. Medicines optimisation and clinical pharmacy support: Process administrative correspondence relating to weight management services, contraception services, Pharmacy First referrals and provision of cannabis therapy letters. Add medication information and relevant coding to patient records in accordance with practice protocols and escalate any clinical concerns or treatment decisions to the Pharmacy Technician or Clinical Pharmacist team. Liaise with Pharmacy Technicians regarding monitoring requirements before medication reviews. Assist with the preparation and booking of Structured Medication Reviews. Process non-complex medication-related correspondence in accordance with practice protocols. Liaise with pharmacies on the supply of prescribed drugs, alert our clinicians of any supply issues and forward information on the recommended alternative. Respond to enquiries from patients, carers, secretaries, NHS administrators, Consultants or the Medicines Management Team in a courteous, timely and efficient manner, by telephone, letter and email, occasionally face-to-face and maintain precise records of the communications. Support administration of long-term condition clinics and medicines optimisation programmes. Support delivery of medicines optimisation audits and quality improvement projects. Coordinate and support CQC, PQS, internal practice audits and high-risk drug monitoring. Undertake monthly medication ordering audits and reception medication request audits. Assist with data collection, reporting and maintenance of audit trackers. Support the administrative management of MHRA alerts, medication recalls and prescribing safety initiatives. Run searches and reports as requested and maintain accurate records of completed actions. Support the Clinical Pharmacy Team in reviewing and updating the practice prescribing related policies. Support the training of reception and administrative staff in prescription processes, prescribing workflows and pharmacy-related procedures. Contribute to improving pharmacy administrative processes and service delivery. Work collaboratively with Clinical Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians and the wider practice team to support effective patient care. This Job Description is neither exhaustive nor exclusive and will be reviewed periodically in conjunction with the post holder. The post holder is required to carry out any duties that may reasonably be requested by the Partners or the Practice Manager.

title: UCC Receptionist
description: Join our dynamic urgent care team as a Receptionist and Administrator, where you'll be the welcoming and efficient organiser that keeps our center running smoothly. In this vital role, you will handle patient check-ins, manage appointment scheduling, and ensure seamless communication between patients and healthcare providers. Your energetic approach will help create a welcoming environment while maintaining accurate administrative records. This position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to high-quality urgent care services in a fast-paced setting. This is an exciting opportunity to join a rapidly growing GP-led provider organisation at a pivotal point in its development. The post holder will be responsible for administering the Urgent Care Centre (UCC) service located in the Royal Berkshire Hospital, including registering patients, managing the appointment book, coordinating with clinicians, management, and other administrative staff to ensure the effective running of the service. The post holder will be familiar with EMIS, or another clinical IT systems used in NHS primary care, although additional training will be provided. The post holder will answer telephone calls from patients, staff, and external providers (e.g. 111, emergency department (ED) or other hospital departments), respond to queries, provide information, and communicate about the UCC service in a clear, professional, and effective manner. The post holder will ensure that administrative and clerical duties are carried out according to the relevant policies, procedures, and guidelines. The post holder may be required to provide administrative support with other tasks in the areas of governance and reporting, for example by completing data entry tasks. Excellent customer service is key to this role to build effective working relationships and ensure a good patient experience. The post holder will: Be a key member of the UCC service team, supporting the effective delivery of the service. Act as the first point of contact for patients arriving at the service, registering them in the clinical IT system (EMIS) and providing relevant information. Be responsible for the shared mailbox during operational hours, responding or directing queries appropriately and professionally. Respond professionally to all queries or direct the query to another member of the team, as appropriate. Keep accurate records of contacts with patients, whether in person or by telephone, updating patient records in EMIS with relevant information. Contact patients who have not arrived for their appointments. Create and send discharge summaries and other clinical documentation to patients own GP practices. Make outbound calls to GP practices and other health professionals, providing relevant information to ensure seamless handover to other services. Complete data entry and other related administrative tasks, for example, completing incident reports and updating contact information, following the relevant processes and guidelines. Escalate issues through appropriate channels, communicating clearly with clinicians and management to resolve problems in a timely and effective manner. Assisting with the preparation of audits and reports under the direction of the Admin Team Leader. Provide cover for other members of the team where required, working flexibly to meet operational objectives. Supporting and attending team meetings as needed. Be flexible and adaptable to meet the needs of the organisation. Any other task commensurate with the role as directed.
